content.title: About
content.content: Whiting (Merlangius merlangus), also known as picarel, is a marine fish of the cod family that inhabits the coastal waters of the Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea. It has a light, firm flesh with a mild flavor, low fat content and high protein levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting can change its skin colour to blend with the surrounding water, becoming paler in open sea.
In Europe, whiting is a traditional ingredient in fish‑and‑chips and other classic dishes.
Wild individuals may reach up to 70 cm and over 3 kg, but most commercial catches are 30–45 cm long.
The species migrates seasonally, moving to warmer coastal waters in summer for spawning.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Whiting provides about 18 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The fish contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Whiting is a source of selenium, iodine and phosphorus, nutrients that support immune function and thyroid health.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in oily fish, whiting still provides modest amounts of EPA and DHA, beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including whiting.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Coastal fish can accumulate mercury and cadmium; choose products from reputable suppliers.

items.title: Food poisoning
items.content: Improper storage or insufficient cooking can allow bacterial growth leading to foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Whiting can be baked, boiled, pan‑fried or steamed. It is often breaded and fried to a golden crust. The mild flesh pairs well with lemon, fresh herbs (parsley, dill) and light sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh fillets should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and used within 2 days. Frozen whiting can be stored at –18 °C for 3‑4 months. Before cooking, check the smell: it should be clean, sea‑like, without a strong ammonia odor.
